intended_object: A local shorthand for the associated graded module (with respect to the order filtration) of the quotient A_{n+1}/I of the presented Weyl algebra by one specific "canonical" right ideal I, built from d and N. It is used inside the project's proof of Stafford's theorem. I inferred this from the docstring and from how the file uses it.
explanation: The `abbrev` adds no new mathematics. It just applies the library's own `OrderAssociatedGradedModule` to the project-specific ideal `presentedCanonicalRightIdeal n N d`. That ideal is `canonicalRightIdeal (presentedCoordinate k n) d N`, an auxiliary ideal that exists only for this proof. The same expression appears written out with `let E := ...` in `CanonicalOldTangentialFiniteness.lean`. In this file the abbreviation's only role is to carry local instances: right after it come a tangential polynomial `Module` instance and some equivalences. So it is a notational device for an intermediate proof object, not a standalone mathematical notion that could be judged against the literature. The body does match its docstring: it is the order-associated graded module of the canonical right-ideal quotient.
